pleased to announce the audited results for the year ended 31st December 2022. The same accounting policies and methods of computation have been used as were in the last financial statements. Business commentary The Group’s turnover for the year ended 31 December 2022 grew by 6% (KShs 656 million) to KShs 11.4 billion in comparison with year 2021 which had a 17% (KShs 1.54 billion) increase to KShs 10.7 billion against the year 2020. The operating profit before tax, for year ended 31 December 2022 declined by 5% (KShs 51 million) to KShs 1.07 billion compared to the year ended 31 December 2021 where a 30% (KShs 262 million) growth to KShs 1.12 billion was attained against the year ended 31 December 2020. In 2022, the drop in profitability is due to unfavourable foreign exchange rates, high cost of raw materials and the slow down in economic activities during the year. The global economy was characterized by fluctuating currency exchange rates and rising prices of essential raw materials, such as oil, which had a severe impact on businesses across various industries. Crown Paints was not spared and the high cost of raw materials led to an increase in production costs and hence a decrease in profit margins. The weakening of Kenyan Shilling against the US Dollar and other major world currencies made it more expensive to import raw materials, and this, in turn, impacted the cost of production.The Board is optimistic that the business of the Group will improve in 2023 as the world economies are improving. DIVIDEND The Board of Directors recommend payment of KShs 4.00 (2021: KShs 4.00) per share as final dividend for the year. By Order of the Board Conrad Nyukuri, Company secretary 26th April 2023
